claim: Evaluate a simple business model through user value, corporate culture, management integrity, long-run economics and opportunity cost.

Opportunity cost expressed as an amount of money rather than a rate: the interest the whole purchase price would have earned in high-grade corporate bonds over the same five years the cash-flow fact covers. Stating it in currency lets the comparison be made against the cash the business actually produced, with no annualisation on either side.

The share of the gross margin that survives everything the company does with it. Gross margin is evidence that the right thing was made; how much of it reaches the owner is evidence about whether it was then done well.
Decline when the long-run money-making mechanism cannot be explained.
Reject on a human-adjudicated material integrity breach.
Reject when revenue growth lacks public evidence of durable user value.
Excluded claim: private views or holdings
Excluded claim: culture scores invented by the model
Excluded claim: translation of informal posts into hard thresholds without adjudication
Known limit: Signed social posts are conversational, editable and unevenly archived; authorship and context require manual review.
Known limit: Public holdings do not reveal purchase price, full rationale, portfolio constraints or current intent.
